city-bus.definition: A bus that carries passengers around a city or nearby suburbs along regular routes and schedules.

double-decker.definition: A bus with two passenger levels, one above the other.
double-decker.exampleUsage: A double-decker waited at the city bus station.

coach.definition: A bus designed for longer journeys, usually with comfortable seating.

minibus.definition: A small bus that carries fewer passengers than a full-sized bus.

shuttle.definition: A bus service that travels repeatedly between specific places.

school-bus.definition: A vehicle built or modified to carry students between school and activities connected with it.

trolley.definition: An electric bus powered through overhead wires.

articulated-bus.definition: A long bus made of two or more sections joined by a flexible connection.
articulated-bus.exampleUsage: The articulated bus can carry many passengers.

night-bus.definition: A bus service that operates late at night or during overnight hours.
night-bus.exampleUsage: The night bus runs after the subway closes.

express-bus.definition: A bus that travels more quickly by making fewer stops than a regular service.
express-bus.exampleUsage: The express bus stops only at major stations.

platform.definition: A designated area where passengers board or leave buses.

shelter.definition: A covered place that protects people while they wait for a bus.

bench.definition: A long seat for more than one person.

ticket-booth.definition: A place where visitors buy or collect tickets.

schedule.definition: A list of planned bus departure and arrival times.

map.definition: A drawing that shows places, routes, and geographical features.

vending-machine.definition: A machine that dispenses products after a customer inserts payment.
vending-machine.exampleUsage: The vending machine was used during the activity.

restroom.definition: A public room containing toilets and washing facilities.

ticket.definition: A printed or electronic document that permits travel on a bus.

pass.definition: A ticket that permits specified bus journeys over a period of time.

fare.definition: The price paid for a journey on public transport.

tap-card.definition: A contactless travel card that is touched against a reader to pay a fare or record a journey.
tap-card.exampleUsage: Passengers tap the card on the reader when boarding.

machine.definition: A device with moving parts that performs a task.

receipt.definition: A written or digital record showing that a payment was made.

zone.definition: An area used to determine the fare for a public-transport journey.

transfer.definition: A change from one bus or transport service to another during a journey.

day-pass.definition: A travel ticket that allows journeys on a transport system for one day.
day-pass.exampleUsage: The day pass covers unlimited bus rides until midnight.

student-discount.definition: A reduced charge that businesses offer people enrolled in school for products or services.

seat.definition: Any support where you can sit (especially the part of a chair or bench etc. on which you sit).

aisle.definition: Passageway between seating areas as in an auditorium or passenger vehicle or between areas of shelves of goods as in stores.

handrail.definition: A fixed rail that passengers hold for support or balance.

bell.definition: A device that makes a ringing sound.
bell.exampleUsage: The bell was used during the activity.

stop-button.definition: A button passengers press to tell the driver they want to leave at the next stop.
stop-button.exampleUsage: She pressed the stop button before her station.

driver-seat.definition: The seat where the driver sits and controls a vehicle.
driver-seat.exampleUsage: The driver seat is separated from the passenger area.

wheelchair-ramp.definition: A sloping platform that allows a wheelchair to enter or leave a bus or building more easily.
wheelchair-ramp.exampleUsage: The driver lowered the wheelchair ramp at the stop.

luggage-rack.definition: A frame or shelf on a bus for storing passengers' bags.

driver.definition: The person who controls and drives the bus.

passenger.definition: A traveler riding in a vehicle (a boat or bus or car or plane or train etc.) who is not operating it.

commuter.definition: A person who regularly travels between home and work or study.

inspector.definition: A transport worker who checks that passengers have valid tickets.

attendant.definition: A worker who assists passengers or provides services at the station.

tourist.definition: A person who travels for pleasure.

student.definition: A person who studies at a school.

elderly.definition: Relating to people who are old, especially those past middle age.

parent.definition: An adult who cares for a child.

child.definition: A young person who has not become an adult.

route-number.definition: A number used to identify a particular public transport route.
route-number.exampleUsage: Check the route number before getting on the bus.

destination-sign.definition: A sign on a vehicle that shows where the service is going.
destination-sign.exampleUsage: The destination sign showed the final station.

timetable.definition: A schedule listing events and the times at which they will take place.

delay-notice.definition: A message informing passengers that a service will arrive or depart later than planned.
delay-notice.exampleUsage: A delay notice appeared on the information screen.

stop-sign.definition: A red, eight-sided road sign requires drivers to halt before crossing an intersection.

bus-lane.definition: A marked section of a road is reserved for buses rather than general traffic.

no-entry.definition: A sign or instruction showing that people or vehicles are not allowed to enter an area.
no-entry.exampleUsage: The no-entry sign blocked access to the bus lane.

next-stop.definition: The next place where a bus, train, or other service is scheduled to stop.
next-stop.exampleUsage: The screen displayed the name of the next stop.

final-stop.definition: The last scheduled stop on a route or journey.
final-stop.exampleUsage: Everyone left the bus at the final stop.

detour.definition: A roundabout road (especially one that is used temporarily while a main route is blocked).
